title: Article 121 — Restriction on discussion in Parliament

content.overview: Article 121 provides that no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President praying for the removal of the Judge as provided in the Constitution.
content.glance: No discussion in Parliament of a Judge’s conduct in discharge of duties, except on a removal-address motion.
content.study:
Article 121 protects judicial independence by restricting parliamentary discussion of the conduct of Supreme Court and High Court Judges in the discharge of their duties. The only exception is a motion for an address to the President praying for removal under the constitutional removal procedure (Articles 124, 217 and related).

Examination: general bar; sole exception = removal-address motion; link to judicial removal procedure.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: No discussion in Parliament on the conduct of any SC or HC Judge in the discharge of his duties, except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President praying for the Judge’s removal as provided in the Constitution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What restriction does Article 121 place on discussion in Parliament?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 121 provides that no discussion shall take place in Parliament with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court in the discharge of his duties, except upon a motion for presenting an address to the President praying for the removal of the Judge as provided in the Constitution.

examTips: No discussion of Judge’s conduct except on removal-address motion.

keyTakeaways: Art 121: bar on discussing Judges’ conduct except removal motion.
